title: Certify a Lean proof through the kernel
when: deciding whether a proof that passed lean_check counts: the orchestrator calls it for every candidate before a claim becomes proved or refuted
re-certifying the proof of a claim against its reference after a change of Lean or of the project
whenNot: checking a proof while it is written: lean_check is faster and shows the errors at their lines
seeing the goals of a proof: lean_goals

original.description: The reference: a Lean file that states the target, with sorry as its proof

candidate.description: The file to certify: the reference with the proof filled in

target.description: The fully qualified name of the theorem the candidate proves

allowedAxioms.description: The axioms the target may depend on, such as propext

timeoutSec.description: The time limit of the whole certification (both compiles and the replay), in seconds

reasons.description: Why the candidate was rejected; empty when it is certified

axioms.description: The axioms the target depends on, sorted

certificate: the candidate was compiled in a fresh process; every declaration of the compiled module was replayed through the kernel (Lean.Environment.replay); the target's axioms, collected from the replayed environment, are all allowed; and the target's type and the definitions it depends on are the reference's, compared as terms (documentation/certifier.md)

input.original:
theorem Harness.add_zero' (n : Nat) : n + 0 = n := by
  sorry
input.candidate:
theorem Harness.add_zero' (n : Nat) : n + 0 = n := by
  rfl

examples.title: a proof that leaves a sorry

reasons: Harness.add_zero' depends on axioms that are not allowed: [sorryAx]

implementations.description: lake env lean in the bench's Lean project (Lean v4.27.0, formal-conjectures at the bench revision): the candidate and the reference are compiled in fresh processes, then lean/SeshatCertify replays them through the kernel. The compile runs the candidate's code as the harness's user unless the host profile gives a sandbox command. Never run against a real Lean yet, and lean/SeshatCertify has never been compiled (documentation/certifier.md).
